magians.name: The Magians
magians.title: The Magians
magians.dict: Named once, in a list of the faiths God will judge between (22:17): the Zoroastrians of Persia.

malik.name: Malik
malik.title: Malik
malik.dict: The keeper of Hell, to whom its people cry, "Let your Lord finish us off"; he answers, "You are staying" (43:77).

mary.name: Mary
mary.title: Mary (Maryam)
mary.dict: The only woman the Quran names, and it names her more often than the New Testament does. Dedicated to God before her birth and raised in the sanctuary under Zechariah's care (3:35-37); chosen "over all the women of the world" (3:42). A spirit from God announces a son to her, and she gives birth alone beneath a palm tree (19:16-26). Surah 19 bears her name. Most of the verses listed here name her in the phrase "Jesus son of Mary".

michael.name: Michael
michael.title: Michael (Mikal)
michael.dict: Named once, beside Gabriel: God is an enemy to whoever is an enemy to His angels and messengers, to Gabriel and Michael (2:98).

moses.name: Moses
moses.title: Moses (Musa)
moses.dict: The person the Quran names most: 136 times, in 34 surahs. His story is told again and again, in pieces: the infant set adrift and taken in by Pharaoh's household, the man he kills, his years in Midian (28:3-28); the fire and the voice, "I am God" (20:9-48); the staff, the magicians, the plagues and the sea (7:103-137, 26:10-68); the mountain, the tablets and the calf (7:142-156, 20:83-98). God "spoke to Moses directly" (4:164), and the Book given to him is called a guide and a light (5:44).

muhammad.name: Muhammad
muhammad.title: Muhammad
muhammad.dict: The one to whom the Quran is addressed throughout, mostly as "you", "the Messenger" or "the Prophet". He is named only four times as Muhammad (3:144, 33:40, 47:2, 48:29) and once as Ahmad, in the words of Jesus (61:6); the verses listed here are those, and the verses that address him "O Prophet" or "O Messenger". He is "no more than a messenger" (3:144), "a human being like you" (18:110), "the seal of the prophets" (33:40), and sent "as mercy to mankind" (21:107). The events of his life are known from the early biographies, not from the Quran.
